newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to help Mozambique clear landmines.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to help Mozambique clear landmines.

text.p: South Africa and neighbouring Mozambique signed an agreement on Wednesday to lift landmines littered around villages in Mozambique's Maputo province.
The South African Foreign Affairs Department said in a statement that Mechem, a subsidiary of state-owned arms manufacturer Denel, would conduct the mine-clearing operations. It did not say when.

Mechem recently completed a year-long contract for the United Nations in Angola, one of the most heavily mined countries in the world, which opened about 4,600 km (2,875 miles) of road between all provincial capitals.
The company has also lifted mines in Mozambique's Sofala and Manica provinces.

The department said the latest agreement was signed between the foreign ministers of the two countries in Togo, where both are attending a special Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit to end the rebel war in Zaire.
"This agreement follows the recent announcement by both governments banning the use of antipersonnel landmines," the statement said.

The department said there were an estimated two million landmines in Mozambique, left over from the country's 16-year civil war between the Frelimo government and Renamo rebels. The war ended with democratic elections in 1994.
